nodes.title: Atlas
nodes.subtitle: Identity & access management
nodes.body: Atlas is Acme's identity and access management product: single sign-on, multi-factor authentication, and automated user lifecycle provisioning. It is the system of record for who can access what across the Acme suite.

nodes.title: Sentry
nodes.subtitle: Endpoint & zero-trust access
nodes.body: Sentry manages the laptop and device fleet and provides zero-trust remote access to internal applications. It continuously evaluates device posture and gates access based on user role and compliance state.

nodes.title: FlowDesk
nodes.subtitle: Operations, expenses & procurement
nodes.body: FlowDesk is Acme's back-office operations suite covering expenses, travel, and procurement. It auto-categorizes spend, routes approvals, and matches invoices to purchase orders.

nodes.title: SSO Setup Guide
nodes.subtitle: Atlas
nodes.body: Configure single sign-on by registering Acme as a SAML 2.0 or OIDC application in your identity provider. Copy the Atlas ACS URL and entity ID into the provider, then upload the provider's metadata XML back into Atlas. SSO enforcement can be scoped per team, and break-glass local accounts remain available for administrators.

nodes.title: MFA Policy
nodes.subtitle: Atlas
nodes.body: Multi-factor authentication is required for all administrator and finance roles. Atlas supports TOTP authenticator apps, hardware security keys (FIDO2/WebAuthn), and push approval. Users have a 14-day grace period to enroll a second factor before access is blocked.

nodes.title: API Reference
nodes.subtitle: Atlas
nodes.body: The Acme REST API authenticates with a Bearer token scoped to a single workspace. Endpoints are versioned under /v1 and return JSON with cursor-based pagination. Rate limits are 600 requests per minute per token, and webhooks deliver near-real-time events for provisioning and device changes.

nodes.title: Zero-Trust Remote Access
nodes.subtitle: Sentry
nodes.body: Remote employees connect through the Sentry zero-trust gateway rather than a legacy VPN concentrator. Access to internal applications is granted per-request based on device posture and user role. Sessions are re-evaluated every 15 minutes and revoked automatically if the device falls out of compliance.

nodes.title: Device Enrollment Guide
nodes.subtitle: Sentry
nodes.body: Enroll a laptop by installing the Sentry agent and signing in with your Atlas credentials. Enrollment records the device serial number, disk-encryption state, and OS patch level. Devices that fail the posture check are quarantined until they are remediated.

nodes.title: Incident Response Runbook
nodes.subtitle: Sentry
nodes.body: When an alert fires, the on-call responder acknowledges it in the console within 15 minutes and opens an incident channel. Classify severity, contain the affected systems, and record a timeline of actions taken. A blameless post-mortem is required for every Sev-1 and Sev-2 incident within five business days.

nodes.title: Expense Policy
nodes.subtitle: FlowDesk
nodes.body: Employees submit expenses within 30 days of purchase with an itemized receipt attached. Travel over $500 requires manager pre-approval, and any personal charges must be flagged for reimbursement to the company. FlowDesk auto-categorizes line items and routes anything above the department threshold for a second approval.

nodes.title: Procurement Workflow
nodes.subtitle: FlowDesk
nodes.body: A new vendor purchase starts with a procurement request that captures the budget line, business justification, and preferred supplier. Requests above $10,000 route to finance and security review before a purchase order is issued. FlowDesk tracks the request from approval through invoice matching.

nodes.title: SSO Rollout
nodes.body: Goal: ship SAML and OIDC single sign-on across all three products with per-team enforcement. Status: in progress — Atlas is GA, Sentry is in beta, FlowDesk is scoped for next quarter.

nodes.title: MFA Hardening
nodes.body: Goal: make phishing-resistant MFA (WebAuthn) the default for all privileged roles. Status: in progress — WebAuthn support shipped, org-wide enforcement rollout pending.

nodes.title: Device Fleet MDM
nodes.body: Goal: manage the full laptop fleet through Sentry with automated posture and disk-encryption checks. Status: on track — roughly 70% of devices enrolled.

nodes.title: Zero-Trust Remote Access
nodes.body: Goal: replace the legacy VPN concentrator with the Sentry zero-trust gateway. Status: piloting with two customers; general rollout in planning.

nodes.title: Incident Response Automation
nodes.body: Goal: automate alert triage and incident-channel creation to cut mean time to respond. Status: in progress — runbook automation running in staging.

nodes.title: Expense Flow Redesign
nodes.body: Goal: rebuild the FlowDesk expense submission flow with auto-categorization and mobile receipt capture. Status: design complete, build starting this sprint.

nodes.title: Procurement ERP Integration
nodes.body: Goal: integrate procurement requests with the finance ERP for automated purchase-order issuance. Status: blocked on ERP sandbox access.

nodes.title: New-Hire Onboarding Automation
nodes.body: Goal: auto-provision accounts, devices, and role-based access on day one for every new hire. Status: in progress — dependent on the SSO rollout.

nodes.title: Cedar Retail Group

nodes.title: Orbital Media

nodes.title: Adopt SAML SSO across all internal apps
nodes.subtitle: Single identity provider via Atlas Identity
nodes.body: We will standardize on SAML-based single sign-on through Atlas Identity as the sole identity provider for internal applications. Consolidating logins reduces credential sprawl and gives us one place to enforce access policy. Per-app local accounts will be migrated and disabled once SSO coverage reaches 95%.

nodes.title: Enforce MFA on all admin accounts
nodes.subtitle: TOTP plus WebAuthn required
nodes.body: All administrative and privileged accounts must enroll in multi-factor authentication using TOTP with a WebAuthn hardware-key option. Admin credentials are the highest-value target and password-only access is no longer acceptable. Non-compliant accounts will be locked out after a two-week grace period.

nodes.title: Mandatory MDM enrollment for all laptops
nodes.subtitle: Managed via Sentry Endpoint
nodes.body: Every company laptop must be enrolled in mobile device management through Sentry Endpoint before it can access corporate resources. This gives us inventory, patch enforcement, and remote-wipe for lost devices. Unenrolled devices will be blocked at the access layer.

nodes.title: Replace legacy VPN with zero-trust broker
nodes.subtitle: Per-session, identity-aware access
nodes.body: We will retire the flat legacy VPN in favor of a zero-trust access broker that grants per-application, identity-aware sessions. The old VPN gives implicit network-wide trust once connected, which is our biggest lateral-movement risk. Rollout is phased by team, starting with engineering.

nodes.title: Data retention policy: logs 90 days, PII 24 months
nodes.subtitle: Tiered retention by data class
nodes.body: Operational logs are retained for 90 days and personally identifiable information for a maximum of 24 months, after which records are purged or anonymized. Indefinite retention increases both breach blast-radius and compliance exposure. Exceptions require documented legal-hold approval from data governance.

nodes.title: URL-based API versioning with 6-month deprecation window
nodes.subtitle: /v1, /v2 path prefixes
nodes.body: Public APIs will use URL-path versioning (/v1, /v2) with a guaranteed six-month deprecation window before any version is removed. Path-based versions are explicit and easy for integrators to reason about compared to header negotiation. Deprecations are announced in the changelog and via response headers.

nodes.title: Automate incident-response runbooks in Flowdesk Ops
nodes.subtitle: Codified detection-to-remediation flows
nodes.body: Incident-response runbooks will be codified and automated inside Flowdesk Ops so that common detections trigger consistent, auditable remediation steps. Manual, tribal-knowledge response is too slow and varies by on-call engineer. Every automated action is logged for post-incident review.

nodes.title: Blameless SEV-1 post-mortem process
nodes.subtitle: Mandatory review within 5 business days
nodes.body: Every SEV-1 security incident requires a blameless post-mortem completed within five business days, focused on systemic fixes rather than individual fault. A no-blame culture surfaces the real causes and improves reporting speed. Action items are tracked to closure and reviewed monthly.

nodes.title: Integrate procurement with ERP for PO approvals
nodes.subtitle: Automated purchase-order routing
nodes.body: Procurement will be integrated directly with the ERP so purchase-order approvals route automatically based on amount and cost center. Manual email approvals cause delays and leave a weak audit trail. Thresholds and approver chains are configured centrally by finance ops.

nodes.title: Expense redesign: auto-categorization and travel per-diem
nodes.subtitle: Fewer manual line items
nodes.body: The expense workflow is redesigned to auto-categorize card transactions and apply standardized per-diem rates for travel instead of itemized meal receipts. This cuts submission time and reviewer load while improving policy consistency. Per-diem rates are maintained per region and reviewed twice a year.

nodes.title: Day-1 access provisioning via Atlas Identity groups
nodes.subtitle: Role-driven onboarding automation
nodes.body: New hires receive their baseline application access automatically on day one, driven by role-mapped Atlas Identity groups from the HR system. Manual ticket-based provisioning left people idle and access inconsistent. Role-to-group mappings are owned by each department lead.

nodes.title: Remote-work eligibility and equipment stipend policy
nodes.subtitle: Role-based remote tiers
nodes.body: We formalize remote-work eligibility into role-based tiers and provide a one-time home-office equipment stipend for eligible employees. Ad-hoc arrangements created fairness and budgeting inconsistencies. Eligibility and stipend amounts are documented in the HR handbook.

nodes.title: Deprecate password-only login by Q3
nodes.subtitle: Phased move to SSO plus MFA
nodes.body: Password-only authentication will be fully deprecated by the end of Q3 in favor of SSO with mandatory MFA. Standalone passwords remain the weakest link even with complexity rules. The cutover is phased by application criticality with fallback support during migration.

nodes.title: Enforce full-disk encryption on managed devices
nodes.subtitle: Verified through Sentry Endpoint
nodes.body: Full-disk encryption is mandatory on all MDM-managed devices and its status is continuously verified through Sentry Endpoint. An unencrypted lost or stolen laptop is a reportable data-exposure event. Devices reporting disabled encryption are automatically quarantined from access.

nodes.title: Quarterly least-privilege access reviews
nodes.subtitle: Role-based access recertification
nodes.body: Access grants are reviewed quarterly against a least-privilege baseline, with managers recertifying each report's roles. Access tends to accumulate over time as people change teams, creating standing risk. Grants not recertified within the window are automatically revoked.

nodes.title: Encrypt data at rest with KMS-managed keys
nodes.subtitle: Centralized key lifecycle
nodes.body: All persistent data stores must be encrypted at rest using centrally managed KMS keys with enforced rotation. Application- or disk-level ad-hoc encryption made key custody and rotation unauditable. Key access is scoped per service and logged for governance review.

nodes.title: Sales-to-support handoff SLA for enterprise
nodes.subtitle: 4-hour first response
nodes.body: Enterprise accounts handed from sales to support get a guaranteed four-hour first-response SLA on their initial tickets. Slow early responses after signing eroded trust with our largest customers. Handoffs include an account context packet so support avoids re-discovery.

nodes.title: Schedule v1 API deprecation with migration guide
nodes.subtitle: Client-facing sunset plan
nodes.body: Legacy /v1 API endpoints are placed on a published sunset schedule accompanied by a client migration guide to /v2. Keeping two major versions indefinitely doubles our maintenance and support surface. Integrators receive deprecation headers and proactive support outreach before cutoff.

nodes.title: Identity & Access review
nodes.subtitle: SSO, MFA, password deprecation
nodes.body: Reviewed the identity roadmap: standardizing on SAML SSO, enforcing MFA on admin accounts, and setting a timeline to retire password-only login.

nodes.title: Endpoint & Network security sync
nodes.subtitle: MDM, VPN replacement, disk encryption
nodes.body: Aligned on mandatory MDM enrollment, replacing the legacy VPN with a zero-trust broker, and enforcing full-disk encryption on managed devices.

nodes.title: Data governance council
nodes.subtitle: Retention and encryption at rest
nodes.body: Set tiered data-retention windows and agreed to encrypt all data at rest under centrally managed KMS keys.

nodes.title: API platform planning
nodes.subtitle: Versioning and deprecation
nodes.body: Decided on URL-based API versioning with a six-month deprecation window and scheduled the v1 sunset with a client migration guide.

nodes.title: Incident response tabletop
nodes.subtitle: Runbooks and post-mortems
nodes.body: Walked through a SEV-1 scenario; agreed to automate response runbooks in Flowdesk Ops and to require blameless post-mortems.

nodes.title: Quarterly access & GTM sync
